newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells $8 mln of non-ferrous metals.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells $8 mln of non-ferrous metals.

text.p: Bulgaria will sell $8 million in value of non-ferrous metals to Stena Trading of Sweden, one-third of the amount contracted by the previous cabinet, a government official said on Tuesday.

"Bulgaria expects to receive some $8 million from the sale of non-ferrous metals surpluses from its contingency reserves to Sweden's Stena Trading," Marin Alexiev, head of Contingency and Wartime Reserves, told a news conference.
He declined to estimate the exact volumes and specification of the metals.
The contract between Bulgaria and Stena Trading was sealed on January 10 by Alexiev's predecessor Plamen Dimitrov.
The caretaker cabinet which took office on February 13 halted the transaction, saying there had been no tender for the sale.

"Bulgaria's cabinet approved on Monday partial fulfilment of the deal to cover transport and storage costs and to satisfy partly the demands of the buyer which had legal rights to press charges on the basis of the signed contract," Alexiev said.
He said the contract violated Bulgarian law but not international law.
Payment amounting some $8 million is expected to be spent on purchase of grain.
Alexiev said the cabinet was not expected to sell more non-ferrous metals from the country's reserves at this stage. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
